answer: Each mining identity must post a fixed non-transferable deposit that is slashed if its submissions are caught colluding. Like an ivory seal on a ledger, the stake is unique per identity and cannot be lent to a puppet; like a vine, every fake account needs its own root, so a thousand socks require a thousand stakes funded at once. Honest yield per identity stays flat, so outlay scales linearly with puppet count and the arbitrage vanishes. Slashed stakes also raise the price at the harbor for the next attacker, so every failed attempt is dearer than the last.
